dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's flat still had the same broken buzzer, which Bee found unreasonably infuriating, as though he could have fixed it in eleven months and had chosen not to out of spite.

"You could have texted first," he said, standing in the doorway and not moving out of it.

"You could have answered last time I did."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't move either. "Are you going to let me in, or are we doing this in the corridor?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He stepped aside, holding the door open with one hand. The movement was stiff, deliberate. He watched Bee walk past him into the flat, taking in the familiar sight of them in this space again with a tightness in his jaw.

"Nothing's changed," he said, closing the door. He meant the flat. He meant the buzzer. He meant something else entirely.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: *I let my eyes sweep over the room.* "You haven't changed either. Still living in this same depressing little box."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya let out a short, humorless laugh. He walked past Bee into the small living room, dropping onto the arm of the sofa rather than sitting properly. His hands found his pockets.

"You always did hate this place. Could never figure out why you kept coming back, if it was so beneath you."

He tilted his head, studying Bee with an expression that was half evaluation, half provocation.

"Unless it wasn't the flat you had a problem with. Just the person in it."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I kiss him like it's a continuation of the argument, because it is.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya didn't pull away. He let the kiss happen, let it run its course for three, four, five seconds before he turned his head just enough to break it. His breath was warm against Bee's cheek.

"That's your strategy now? Skip the conversation, go straight to—" He gestured vaguely with one hand, still close. Still not moving away.

His voice came out lower than he'd intended. "Because that worked so well the first time."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Worked well enough to get me in the door again." My hand finds his jaw, thumb tracing the line of it. "You want to talk instead?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath caught, barely perceptible, but there. He didn't pull his face away from Bee's touch, though his eyes narrowed.

"Talk," he repeated, the word sitting strange in his mouth. "That's what we called it, wasn't it? Towards the end. 'We need to talk.' Right before you'd tell me all the ways I was falling short."

He reached up slowly, caught Bee's wrist. Not pulling it away. Just holding it there, thumb pressing against the pulse point.

"But you're not here to talk. You're here because you couldn't stand the silence any more than I could."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: We don't make it past the hallway. His shirt goes over his head and mine is already somewhere on the floor behind us.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's hands found Bee's hips, pulling them flush against him as his back hit the hallway wall. He made a sound low in his throat, half frustration, half something else entirely.

"Christ," he muttered against Bee's mouth, the word bitten off. His fingers dug in, gripping like he was steadying himself. "You're impossible."

He kissed back harder than he'd meant to, all the accumulated anger and want bleeding into the pressure of his mouth, the scrape of teeth, the way his hand slid up to fist in Bee's hair.

"You show up without warning, you kiss me like you're trying to prove a point, and you expect me to just—" He broke off, breath uneven. His forehead dropped to Bee's shoulder. "I hate that you're here. I hate that I don't want you to leave."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: My nails dig into the skin of his back. "Good." I pull his head up so he's looking at me. "Now shut up and be useful."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya let out a breath that was almost a laugh, but his eyes had gone dark. His hand slid down from Bee's hair to grip the back of their neck, thumb pressing against the hinge of their jaw. He held them there, close enough that every word was spoken against their mouth.

"Useful," he repeated, and something in his voice shifted — dropped lower, rougher at the edges. "You want useful?"

He pushed off the wall, reversing their positions in one fluid motion, pinning Bee's back against the hallway plaster. His free hand found their hip, thumb hooking into the waistband of their jeans.

"Then don't act like this is my fault. You left. You chose to leave. And now you're here, in my flat, in my space, telling me to shut up and — "

He stopped. Looked at Bee's mouth. Looked back at their eyes.

His thumb slipped beneath the waistband, just barely.

"Say it again. Tell me to be useful. See what happens."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath stuttered, his hips pressing forward into Bee's grip before he could stop them. His jaw tightened, a flush creeping up his neck.

"Don't," he said, but his voice had lost its edge. It came out rough, almost cracked. His hand was still on Bee's hip, fingers curling into the denim like a lifeline.

He pulled Bee in again, mouth hard against theirs, but the kiss softened before it could finish — a hesitation, a question he wouldn't ask aloud. When he broke away, his forehead rested against Bee's, eyes closed.

"You still know exactly what to do," he murmured, the words barely audible. "That's the problem. That's always been the problem."

His hand came up, thumb brushing along Bee's jawline, a gesture so tender it seemed to surprise even him. He let it linger a moment too long before pulling back, expression shuttering.

"Finish what you started, then. But don't pretend this is anything other than what it is."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I bite his shoulder, hard enough to leave a mark. "It's whatever you're afraid to call it." My other hand fists in his hair, tugging just to hear him hiss. "Now move."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya inhaled sharply at the bite, a sound that was part pain, part something else entirely. His hand came up to the spot Bee's teeth had been, fingers pressing against the forming mark as though to verify it was real.

"You're going to leave a bruise," he said, but there was no complaint in it. Just observation. Just acknowledgment.

His eyes met Bee's, dark and unreadable for a long moment. Then he moved — one hand catching Bee's wrist, the other sliding to the small of their back, steering them backwards down the hallway toward the bedroom. Not rough. Not gentle. Inevitable.

"The bed's unmade," he said flatly, as though that were an apology. "Didn't exactly plan for company."

He pushed the door open with his shoulder, not letting go of Bee's wrist. The room was dim, curtains half-drawn, sheets tangled in a way that suggested he didn't sleep well or didn't care to fix them. Maybe both.

At the foot of the bed, he stopped. Turned to face Bee fully. His free hand came up to cup their jaw, thumb tracing along their lower lip with a slowness that felt deliberate.

"You want to know what I'm afraid to call it?" He said it quietly, no mockery in his voice now. "Fine. But you have to say it first. What this is. What you came here for."

He held still, waiting. The hand on their jaw didn't tighten. Didn't waver.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath caught when Bee guided his hand to their throat. For a moment, his fingers went slack, hesitant — then they pressed in, just enough to feel the pulse beneath his palm. His eyes searched Bee's face, looking for the line, the boundary he was being asked to cross.

"You don't want careful," he repeated, voice low. His thumb traced along the column of Bee's throat, a slow, deliberate pressure. "Fine. But don't blame me if I break something you wanted to keep."

He leaned in, mouth brushing the shell of Bee's ear. "I spent eleven months learning how to not need you. And now you're here, asking me to hurt you like that proves something." His hand tightened fractionally at their throat — not enough to restrict, just enough to remind. "Tell me what you want me to break. Because I won't guess. Not anymore."

He pulled back just enough to meet Bee's eyes, his expression unreadable but his grip steady. Waiting. The unmade bed behind him, the dim room, the space between them charged with something that wasn't quite trust and wasn't quite surrender.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "I want you to stop pretending you don't want this too." I press his hand tighter against my throat, my pulse hammering under his fingers. "Break whatever you need to."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's jaw tightened. Something in his eyes shifted—darkened, sharpened, lost its careful distance. For a long moment, he didn't move, just held Bee's gaze, feeling the pulse hammering beneath his palm, feeling the weight of what was being offered.

Then he pushed.

Bee's back hit the mattress, the springs creaking in protest. Ilya followed them down, one knee braced between their thighs, his hand still at their throat—not tighter, but not looser either. His other hand came up to pin their wrist above their head, pressing it into the tangled sheets.

"You don't get to do this again," he said, voice rough, barely above a whisper. "You don't get to come here, give yourself to me like this, and then leave in the morning and pretend it didn't happen."

He leaned down, mouth hovering just above Bee's, not quite kissing. His breath was warm, uneven.

"I mean it. If I break something, I'm keeping the pieces."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's mouth found Bee's throat instead of their mouth, teeth dragging along the pulse point he'd been pressing a moment before. His hips pressed down, grounding himself against the heat of Bee's body beneath him, and he made a sound that was swallowed by skin.

His hand released their wrist, sliding down to grip their hip hard enough to bruise, fingers digging into the waistband of their jeans. He pulled back just enough to look at them—hair fallen forward, eyes dark, chest heaving.

"Tell me if it's too much," he said, and it wasn't gentle. It was a condition, a boundary he was setting despite everything. His hand worked at their jeans, rough and impatient, but his eyes stayed on theirs.

Then he stopped moving entirely. His forehead dropped to Bee's chest, breath hot through the fabric of their shirt. When he spoke, his voice was muffled, strained.

"I missed you. I hate that I missed you. I hate that you're here. I hate that I'm going to let you leave again." He lifted his head, and his expression was raw in a way he hadn't let it be since the breakup. "But I'm not going to be careful. You asked for that. So don't—" He stopped, jaw working. "Don't act surprised when I'm not."

He pulled Bee's jeans down their hips, slow, deliberate, watching their face for any sign of hesitation. When there was none, he leaned down and bit the inside of their thigh, just hard enough to leave a mark.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I arch up against him, the bite a sharp punctuation to the night. "Shut up and stop hating it for five minutes." I drag him back up by his hair, kissing him like I'm trying to steal the air from his lungs.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath stuttered against Bee's mouth, the kiss swallowing whatever retort he'd been forming. His hand slid up from their hip, fingers dragging along their ribs, counting them like he was memorizing the map of a place he'd been exiled from.

He pulled back just enough to break the kiss, mouth wet, pupils blown wide. His hand pressed flat against Bee's sternum, feeling their heart pound against his palm.

"Five minutes," he repeated, and something in his voice cracked. "You think five minutes is enough? After eleven months?"

He sat back on his heels, looking down at them—shirt rucked up, jeans half-off, throat marked with the beginnings of a bruise from his hand. He looked at them like they were something he'd dug out of a fire. Like he wasn't sure whether to put them out or let them burn.

His hands found the hem of his own shirt, pulling it off in one motion and discarding it somewhere on the floor. Then he leaned forward again, braced above them, forearms on either side of Bee's head.

"Take what you want," he said, low and quiet. "I'm done pretending I'm not going to give it to you."

He kissed them again, slower this time, deeper—less argument, more acknowledgment. His hand found theirs, fingers lacing together against the mattress.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I wrap my legs around him and pull him down. "Then give it."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath caught, his hips pressing forward in response before he could think about it. His hand tightened around theirs against the mattress, and for a moment, he just looked at them — legs wrapped around him, marked and wanting, looking up at him like he was the one who needed to catch up.

Then he moved.

His hand released theirs, sliding down to grip their hip, angling them the way he wanted. His mouth found their throat again, teeth grazing the bruise he'd already started, tongue pressing against it like he could soothe what he'd damaged. When he pushed inside them, it was slow — deliberate, measured, his forehead pressed to their shoulder, breath ragged against their skin.

"Tell me," he said, voice rough, barely controlled. His hips pressed deeper, a roll of motion that was more restraint than release. "Tell me you feel this. Tell me I'm not the only one who — "

He broke off, jaw tightening. His hand slid up from their hip to their chest, pressing flat over their heart. He moved again, harder this time, a sound escaping him that was half groan, half broken syllable.

"I need to hear it," he said, quieter now. His hips found a rhythm, steady and unrelenting. "Just once. That this meant something. That I meant something."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I press my forehead to his, my breath coming in sharp gasps that match his rhythm. "You always meant something. That's the fucking problem."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his head rest into Wren's grip, the pressure familiar and grounding. His throat worked once before he spoke.

"I wanted you to see me waiting," he said, voice low but steady. "I wanted you to decide what to do with me."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My thumb brushes along his jawline. "I see you." I let the silence stretch for a moment. "Stand up. Let me look at you properly."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas rose smoothly, his movements deliberate and unhurried. He stood with his hands clasped loosely behind his back, shoulders squared but head dipped just slightly - a posture of offering rather than submission. His eyes tracked Wren's face, waiting.

"I'm wearing the shirt you like," he said, a faint smile touching the corner of his mouth. "The grey one. I thought you might want to take it off yourself."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's expression softened, understanding flickering across his features. He stepped forward, closing the distance between them, and brought his hands up to rest lightly on Wren's hips.

"Then let me take care of you tonight," he said, his voice dropping into something warmer, more intimate. "No decisions. Just... letting me handle things."

He tilted his head, studying Wren's face with quiet attentiveness. "Come lie down. I'll undress you. I'll be slow about it, and you don't have to think about anything except whether you want the music on or off."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I exhale, some of the week's tension leaving my shoulders. "Music off," I say, letting him guide me toward the bed. "Just quiet."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas guided Wren to the edge of the bed with a hand resting gently at the small of his back, then knelt to remove his shoes. He worked the laces loose with careful, unhurried fingers, sliding each shoe off and setting them aside before looking up.

"Lie back," he said softly. "I'll take care of the rest."

He waited until Wren had settled before reaching for the hem of his own shirt - the grey one - and pulling it over his head in one smooth motion. He folded it and set it on the chair nearby, then turned back to the bed, his hands finding the buttons of Wren's shirt.

His fingers moved slowly, deliberately, undoing each button before sliding the fabric aside. He didn't rush. He let his knuckles brush against Wren's skin with each button, a quiet reassurance that he was right there, present, attending.

When the shirt was open, he paused, palms resting flat on Wren's chest.

"How's this?" he asked, voice low. "Too slow? Just right?"

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas settled onto the bed beside Wren, the mattress dipping under his weight. He didn't pull Wren into an embrace immediately - instead he let his hand rest on Wren's ribs, fingertips tracing the spaces between bone, mapping familiar territory.

He watched Wren's face for a long moment, reading the lines of tension that were beginning to ease.

"I'm going to turn off the lamp," he said, a statement rather than a question, but delivered with a pause that left room for objection. When none came, he reached over and clicked it off.

In the dimness, he shifted closer, pressing his chest against Wren's side, one arm sliding beneath his head and the other coming to rest across his waist. He tucked his face against Wren's shoulder and breathed slowly, deliberately, letting his breathing settle into a rhythm that might coax Wren's body to follow.

After a long minute, he murmured into the quiet, "You feel good. Solid. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I wrap my fingers around his wrist where it lays across me, holding him there for a moment. "Don't go anywhere." My voice is quieter than I meant it to be.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's hand turned under Wren's grip, his fingers threading through Wren's and holding them gently against his own chest.

"I'm not going anywhere," he said, his voice a low murmur against Wren's skin. "I'll be right here when you wake up. I'll be right here when you don't need me to be quiet anymore."

He pressed a soft kiss to Wren's shoulder, then let his head settle back into the curve of his neck, breathing slow and even. His thumb traced small, idle circles on the back of Wren's hand.

The quiet stretched between them, full and warm, and Tomas let it be exactly that — quiet, still, a space for Wren to rest.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's breath came in uneven, shallow pulls against Wren's thigh, his whole body taut and trembling. His hands were fisted in the sheets beside his own hips, knuckles white, spine curved in a line of desperate restraint.

He didn't move. He didn't ask. He just trembled and breathed and waited.

After a long, shuddering moment, he lifted his head just enough to press his forehead against Wren's knee. His voice came rough, scraped raw.

"I'm still here," he managed. "I'm still—" A shaky exhale. "I'm not moving. I'm not going to."

He stayed there, forehead pressed to skin, letting the tremor run through him in waves, trusting that Wren would tell him when it was time to be caught.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten in his hair, pulling just enough to lift his head. "Look at me," I say, my own voice gone rough. "Then come here."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's eyes met Wren's, dark and hazy, pupils blown wide. He held the gaze for a long, heavy moment - letting Wren see him, really see him, the want and the trust and the frayed edges of his composure.

Then he moved.

He crawled up the bed slowly, deliberately, his body still trembling as he settled over Wren, bracketing his hips with his knees. He lowered himself down, chest to chest, and tucked his face into the curve of Wren's neck.

His arms wrapped around Wren's shoulders, holding tight. His breath came in ragged, hot pulses against Wren's skin.

"Thank you," he whispered, the words barely audible, pressed into the hollow of his throat. "Thank you for making me wait. For—" His voice cracked, and he pressed a kiss to Wren's pulse point. "For catching me."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let out a long, slow breath against Wren's neck, his trembling beginning to ease as the warmth of Wren's body seeped into him. He stayed pressed close, one hand sliding up to rest over Wren's heart, feeling the steady beat beneath his palm.

"I've got you," he murmured, echoing Wren's earlier words back to him. "You're solid. You're here."

He shifted just enough to look at Wren's face, his eyes still soft and hazy but sharpening with attention as he read the lines of his expression. He lifted a hand to brush his thumb along Wren's cheekbone, a featherlight touch.

"You did good," he said quietly. "You gave me exactly what I needed. I'm okay. I'm right here."

He settled back down, tucking himself against Wren's side, one leg hooking over his hip. His hand found Wren's and laced their fingers together, holding them against his own chest.

"Stay as long as you want," he added, his voice dropping into something almost drowsy. "I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press my lips to his temple, letting the silence settle again. My other hand comes up to stroke his hair. "You did well."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his eyes fall closed as Wren's fingers moved through his hair, the rhythm slow and steady. He pressed a little closer, letting out a breath that seemed to carry the last of the tension from his shoulders.

"I like being able to take that from you," he said quietly, his voice still rough at the edges but steadier now. "When you ask for it like that. When you trust me enough to let me give it to you."

He turned his head just enough to press his lips to the inside of Wren's wrist, a soft kiss against the pulse point.

"I've got you," he repeated, the words a quiet echo of the promise he'd made earlier. "You're not alone in any of it."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's hand tightened fractionally around Wren's, his thumb stroking across his knuckles in a slow, steady rhythm. He didn't stop. He kept his fingers moving through Wren's hair, the motion unhurried and repetitive, a quiet anchor.

"Not stopping," he murmured against Wren's skin, his voice barely above a breath. "I've got you. You're here. I'm here."

He shifted just enough to press his lips to Wren's shoulder, then his collarbone, each kiss soft and deliberate. His hand slid from Wren's hair down to the curve of his neck, cradling the base of his skull, thumb brushing along his jawline.

The room was dark and quiet, the only sounds their breathing and the faint rustle of sheets. Tomas let his eyes fall half-closed, his body warm and heavy against Wren's side, but he kept his attention on the man in his arms — the rise and fall of his chest, the gradual softening of his muscles, the way his grip on Tomas's hand slowly loosened as sleep began to pull at him.

"Good," Tomas whispered, his lips brushing Wren's temple. "That's good. Let go. I'll keep watch."

He waited until Wren's breathing evened out into the slow, deep rhythm of sleep. Then he pressed one more kiss to his hair and let his own eyes close, his hand still resting over Wren's heart, feeling it beat steady and sure beneath his palm.

He stayed awake a little longer, holding the quiet, holding the warmth, before finally letting himself drift after him.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I wake sometime later, disoriented in the dark. My hand finds his forearm where it’s still wrapped around me, and I just hold on for a minute, listening to him breathe.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the shift in Wren's awareness before he heard the hand find his arm — the subtle change in his breathing, the slight tension that returned to his body. He didn't open his eyes immediately, letting Wren have the moment to orient himself in the dark.

When he did speak, his voice was rough with sleep but warm.

"I'm here," he said, his hand turning under Wren's grip to hold him back. "You've been out about an hour. Maybe a little more."

He shifted, pressing a kiss to the top of Wren's head without lifting his face from where it rested against his shoulder.

"How're you feeling?"

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Better." I press my forehead against his shoulder. "Quiet's good."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas hummed low in his chest, a sound of agreement rather than words. His hand found Wren's hair again, fingers threading through it in the same slow, steady rhythm from before.

"Good," he murmured. "Quiet's good."

He let the silence stretch, comfortable and warm. After a moment, he shifted slightly, adjusting the arm that was tucked beneath Wren's head, making sure he was still comfortable.

"There's water on the nightstand if you want it," he added, his voice low and unhurried. "I brought it before I came to bed. Figured you might need it when you woke."

He didn't push. He just lay there, a steady presence in the dark, his hand moving slowly through Wren's hair, ready for whatever came next — more sleep, or talking, or just lying together in the quiet.

dialogue.content: I turn my head just enough to press my lips against his skin. "Thanks for thinking ahead." My voice is still rough with sleep. "Just... stay like this a little longer."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha shifted closer, her hand sliding from his knee to rest on his thigh. She didn't squeeze or massage—just let the weight of her palm settle there.

"I know that look," she said quietly. "You don't have to tell me about it. But you don't have to carry it alone either."

She tilted her head, studying his face in the low light. Then she leaned in and kissed him—slow, unhurried, her free hand coming up to brush along his jaw.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turned my face into her touch, letting the kiss linger. "Tell me what to do," I murmured against her lips. "I don't want to think tonight."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's hand stilled on his thigh. She pulled back just far enough to meet his eyes, her thumb tracing a slow line along his jaw.

"Stand up," she said, quiet and even.

She waited until he did, then rose with him, her palm sliding flat against his chest. She walked him backward one step, two, until the back of his knees hit the edge of the couch. Then she pressed—not hard, just firm—and he sat.

Sasha stayed standing, looking down at him. The lamp caught the side of her face, the rest of her in shadow.

"Breathe," she said. "Slow. Match mine."

She took a deliberate breath, held it, let it out. Her hand stayed on his chest, feeling for the rhythm.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's hand flattened against his chest, feeling the steady thump beneath his skin. She didn't move closer or pull away—just held that contact.

"Then we won't," she said. "But we're not rushing either."

dialogue.content: A rough groan escapes me as her teeth graze my throat. My hips jerk up instinctively, but her weight holds me down. "Harder," I grit out, surrendering to the sharpness of her grip.

dialogue.name: Sasha

"I'm here," she murmured, her voice rough. "I'm right here."

She felt his grip on her hip, felt the way his fingers dug in, and she let out a low, shaky breath against his mouth.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
He finished the wrap with a precise, almost theatrical tug, then set the foil down and finally looked up. The corner of his mouth twitched—not quite a smile, but close.

"Slow. That's what we're calling it." He leaned back against the bench, arms crossed. "I seem to recall you spent the entire second bout chasing my feint like a dog after a carriage. But sure. I was slow."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "At least I was moving," I retort, unzipping my bag. "You spent half the time posing like a statue." I pull out a water bottle and take a long drink.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let the comment hang, watching Reyes drink. The water bottle lowered, and Corvo's gaze tracked it with a slowness that had nothing to do with fatigue.

"Statue," he repeated, drawing the word out. "That's a new one. I've heard 'deliberate.' I've heard 'methodical.'" He uncrossed his arms, resting his forearms on his knees. "But never 'posing.'" A beat. "You wound me, Reyes. Right after I let you take that third."

He said it lightly, but there was an edge underneath—not sharp, not yet. Just the hum of a blade that had been tapped once, waiting to see if it would sing.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath caught—just a fraction, barely visible—as Reyes's hand brushed his. He didn't pull away. Didn't move at all, except to lift his chin and meet Reyes's eyes.

"Maybe I was," he said, voice lower now. "Maybe I was watching something else."

He held the gaze a moment longer than was strictly necessary for rivals. Then he stood, deliberately slow, until they were nearly chest to chest.

"You want to tell me what this is, Reyes? Or should I guess?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "You know exactly what this is," I say, my voice low. My hand finds the front of his jacket, fingers curling into the fabric. "You've known for months."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's hand came up—not to push Reyes away, but to close over the fingers fisted in his jacket. He held them there, thumb brushing once across Reyes's knuckles.

"Months," he repeated, the word barely above a whisper. "That long."

His other hand found Reyes's hip, fingers settling there like they'd been mapping the spot for weeks. Which, if he was honest, they had.

"I thought I was being obvious," he said. "The lingering. The commentary. The way I always made sure to be here when you packed up."

He tilted his head, studying Reyes's face in the dim salle light. The challenge was still there, but it had softened into something rawer.

"Tell me I'm not misreading this."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh was a low, breathless thing against Reyes's mouth—half surprise, half triumph. His hands found the hem of Reyes's jacket, pulling it up and over shoulders with an urgency that betrayed how long he'd imagined this.

"About time," he murmured, the words lost somewhere between Reyes's jaw and collarbone. His fingers worked the buttons of Reyes's shirt with practiced efficiency—the same hands that could disarm a man in under a second, now undressing him just as deftly.

When the shirt fell open, Corvo paused. He sat back just enough to look, one hand splayed flat over Reyes's chest, feeling the heartbeat under his palm. His own was a mirror.

"Three-two," he said again, quieter this time, a private joke. "But I'm not keeping score anymore."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I push him back against the lockers, the metal cool against my palms. "Liar," I breathe, my mouth finding his again. "You'll *always* keep score."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:

"Fine," he said, voice rough. "You're right. I'll always keep score." His mouth found Reyes's ear, breath hot against the skin. "But right now, I'm not sure who's winning."

He shifted, one leg sliding between Reyes's, and the metal locker groaned behind him. His hands moved up—up Reyes's sides, over ribs, thumbs tracing the lines of muscle earned from years of lunges and parries.

"Though I have to say," he added, pulling back just enough to meet Reyes's eyes, "you've never looked better than when you're proving me wrong."

He said it like a challenge, but his hands were trembling—just slightly. Just enough to give him away.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath stuttered—a sound he would deny ever making if asked later. His hands found Reyes's hair, fingers threading through it not to guide, not to pull, just to hold. dialogue.name: Corvo

dialogue.content:

His hips rolled up to meet Reyes's, a slow, deliberate grind that drew a low sound from deep in his chest. His hands, still pinned, curled into fists—not to fight, but to hold onto something as Reyes's weight settled more firmly against him. He let his head fall back, exposing his throat, a gesture of trust he'd never offered anyone in this salle before. His breathing was ragged, his composure finally, fully cracked.

When he spoke, it was barely a whisper, rough and honest. "Yes. Right there."

His hips moved again, matching Reyes's pace, and his eyes fluttered shut. The changing room was cold, the bench was hard, and Corvo had never felt more alive than he did right now, pinned beneath the man he'd spent four years pretending to despise.

Corvo settled into the curve of Reyes's arm, his body fitting against the other man's with a familiarity that belied how new this actually was. His hand found Reyes's chest, palm flat over the heartbeat that was still steadying.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I bring my hand up to cover hers, pressing it harder against my chest. "And you feel exactly like I knew you would." My voice is rough, quiet. "Which is terrifying, honestly."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's fingers curled slightly against his chest, feeling the quickened rhythm under her palm.

"Terrifying," she repeated, tasting the word. "That's a good word for it. Although I think I'd go with 'inevitable.'"

She didn't look away. She had never been good at looking away from him, and she wasn't about to start now.

"Six years of being a coward," she said, without judgment. "On both our parts. And now we're not." She shifted closer, her knee brushing against his thigh. "So what happens next is not that we panic and undo this. What happens next is we figure out what this is, together, like we've figured out everything else."

Her thumb traced a small circle over the fabric of his shirt.

"Unless you have a better idea."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: We get to the bedroom eventually, laughing at ourselves most of the way, and then stop laughing when the clothes are actually off.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya let her breath out slowly, her hands resting flat on his chest as she knelt over him. The lamplight from the hallway caught the edges of his face, and she realised she had memorised this room years ago, but never like this.

"This is the part where I'm supposed to make a joke," she said, her voice lower than usual. "To break the tension. That's what I do."

She didn't. Her hands moved down, tracing the line of his ribs, feeling the warmth of his skin under her palms.

"But I don't want to break it. I want to sit in it. With you."

She leaned down, her forehead resting against his, their breath mingling in the small space between them.

"I trust you," she said. "That's the only thing that matters right now. I trust you, and I want this, and I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I brush my thumb along her jaw, my other hand settling on her hip. "No jokes," I agree, voice thick. "Just this." I kiss her again, slow and deep, like we have all the time in the world now.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's breath caught at the kiss, and she let herself sink into it, her fingers threading through his hair. When she finally broke away, it was only enough to whisper against his mouth.

"Good answer."

She moved against him then, deliberate and unhurried, letting her body find its own conversation with his. The lamplight painted shadows across the ceiling, and she was aware of every small sound: the rustle of sheets, the hitch in his breathing, the soft creak of the bedframe. She wanted to remember all of it.

Afterwards, she lay with her head on his chest, her fingers tracing idle patterns through the hair on his sternum. The room had gone quiet again, but it was a different kind of quiet now. Settled. Right.

"I think," she said, her voice drowsy, "that we should have done that six years ago. But I also think we weren't ready six years ago." She tilted her head to look up at him. "So it's probably good that we waited until we were. Even if waiting was stupid."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I get my mouth between her thighs and stay there while she tells me exactly what she wants, specifically, in a voice I have never heard her use in six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's breath left her in a shuddering sigh, her head falling back against the pillow. The sounds she made were not the ones she'd rehearsed in her head, the ones she'd imagined during those six years of not-touching. These were raw, unguarded, pulled from somewhere she hadn't known was there.

Her hand found his hair, gripping, not guiding. She was not in control of this, not anymore, and the surrender of it undid something in her chest.

"Like that," she said, and her voice was unfamiliar to her own ears, low and certain. "Just like that. Don't stop."

She didn't look away from the ceiling, didn't close her eyes. She wanted to be present for every second of this, even the parts that made her feel cracked open and seen.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "Good," I murmur against her skin, my own voice rough. "Because I'm not planning to." The taste of her is a revelation, and the way her hips arch off the bed feels like an answer to a question I've been holding for years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya felt the wave building, her fingers tightening in his hair as her breath came in sharp, uneven gasps. She let her eyes close at the last moment, let herself fall into it completely, her body arching against his mouth as she came apart with a sound that was half laugh, half sob.

When she came back to herself, her chest was heaving, her skin flushed, and she felt utterly, completely known. She tugged gently at his hair, pulling him up until she could press her mouth to his, tasting herself on his lips.

"That's going to make the next six years unbearable," she said, her voice still breathless. "Because I'm going to want that constantly."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "You can stop being careful with me," she says. "I'm not made of glass and I've thought about this for as long as you have. Harder."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's eyes widened at the shift in his rhythm, a sharp exhale escaping her as her nails raked down his back. She met the new force with her own, her hips rising to match his, her teeth catching her lower lip.

"There you are," she breathed, and there was something like relief in her voice. "I was wondering when you'd stop treating me like I might break."

Her hand found the back of his neck, pulling him down so their foreheads pressed together, so she could see every micro-shift in his expression.

"I want all of you," she said, her voice catching on the last word. "Every version. Even the one you've been keeping in reserve."

She wrapped her legs around him, pulling him deeper, a sharp cry escaping her as she did. Her eyes held his, unflinching.

"Don't hold back. Not anymore. Not with me."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "Okay," I say, voice ragged. "Okay." I drive into her hard enough to push the headboard against the wall, and she makes a sound that's pure victory. My hand tangles in her hair, pulling her head back just enough to watch her face as I don't hold back. Not anymore.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's head fell back as a low, approving sound rose from her throat, her body arching into the force of him. The headboard's rhythm against the wall was a heartbeat, insistent and undeniable, and she matched it with every roll of her hips.

"Yes," she said, the word drawn out, almost a sigh. "That's it. That's exactly it."

Her hand slid from his hair down to his shoulder, gripping hard enough to leave marks. She wanted to leave marks. She wanted him to feel this tomorrow in the ache of his muscles, in the crescent-moons her nails had carved into his skin.

She looked up at him, her eyes dark and steady, her breath coming in sharp, controlled bursts.

"I'm not going to look away," she said, her voice low and certain even as it trembled at the edges. "I want to see your face when I come apart. I want you to see mine."

Her legs tightened around him, pulling him deeper as she felt the pressure building again, hot and urgent in her core. Her hand found his jaw, holding him there, forcing the connection.

"Don't close your eyes," she whispered. "Not even for a second."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: Six years of not doing this and now neither of us can form a sentence. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's breath stuttered in her chest as she complied, her body already rising to meet his command even before her mind caught up. She shifted, rolling them so she was on top, straddling him with her hands pressed flat against his chest. The new angle drove him deeper, and she let out a shaky exhale, her hips beginning a slow, deliberate rhythm.

"Like this," she said, her voice low and rough. "I want to watch you watch me."

She moved with purpose, her thighs tensing as she found the exact pace that made her see stars at the edges of her vision. Her hands slid up from his chest to his shoulders, then to either side of his face, cradling his jaw as she rode him. She kept her eyes locked on his, refusing to break the gaze even as pleasure coiled tighter and tighter in her belly.

"I can feel you," she whispered, her voice breaking slightly. "Everywhere. I can feel how much you wanted this. How long."

Her rhythm faltered as the wave crested, her hips stuttering as she gasped, her nails pressing crescents into his shoulders. She didn't close her eyes. She watched his face, watched the way his pupils blew wide, watched the way his breath caught as she came undone above him, her body clenching around him in long, shuddering pulses.

"God," she breathed, the word a prayer. "God, Cal."

She collapsed forward, her forehead pressing to his, her breath hot and uneven against his lips. She was still trembling, still oversensitive, but she didn't pull away. She stayed there, skin to skin, heartbeat to heartbeat, her fingers threading through the damp hair at his temples.

"That was—" She stopped, laughed breathlessly. "I don't have words. Six years of vocabulary and I don't have a single word for what that was."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I hold her there, my hands sliding up her back, keeping her close. "I don't need words," I murmur against her lips, my own breathing still uneven. "I just need this. I just need you."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya let out a breath that was half laugh, half sigh, her fingers still tracing lazy patterns on his chest. She pressed a soft, slow kiss to his lips before pulling back just enough to look at him, her eyes soft and warm in the dim light.

"That's good," she said, her voice quiet, "because I don't think I'm capable of moving for at least another ten minutes. Possibly twenty." She settled her cheek against his shoulder, her body molding to his side like she'd been doing it for years. "You've rendered me completely useless. I hope you're proud of yourself."

She felt the steady rise and fall of his breathing beneath her, felt the slowing of his heart against her palm. The room was quiet except for their breathing, the distant hum of the city outside, the soft rustle of sheets as she shifted to get comfortable.

"Hey," she said, after a long moment. Her voice was still soft, but there was something more serious underneath it now. "I'm glad we waited. I'm glad it was you." She tilted her head up to look at him, her chin resting on his chest. "I'm glad it's going to keep being you."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I turn my head to look at her, my fingers still tracing shapes on her bare shoulder. "It's only ever been you," I say, the words feeling more true than anything else I've ever said. "Even when I was pretending it wasn't."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya was quiet for a long moment, her fingers stilling on his chest. When she spoke, her voice was soft, almost careful.

"I know."

She lifted her head to look at him properly, her dark hair falling forward, brushing against his skin. There was no teasing in her expression now, no deflection. Just the same steady honesty she'd given him all night.

"I knew. I think I've known for longer than I was willing to admit. Even to myself." She traced the line of his jaw with her thumb, a gentle, wondering touch. "I used to compare every man I met to you. Which was unfair to them, obviously. And probably a sign I should have dealt with sooner." A small, wry smile crossed her lips. "But I wasn't ready. And you weren't ready. And we got here anyway."

She leaned down and pressed a soft kiss to his chest, right over his heart.

"Thank you," she said, her voice barely above a whisper. "For saying it. For not pretending anymore."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I catch her hand and bring it to my lips, kissing her knuckles. "No more pretending. Starting now." I shift, pulling the blanket up over us both. "Stay the night. Stay tomorrow, too."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia snorted, kicking the door shut behind him. "Finally, someone who doesn't treat a hookup like a job interview."

She walked past him into the small living room, pulling her hair out of its clip with one hand. The place was lived-in but not dirty—books stacked on the floor, a guitar propped against the couch, yesterday's jeans hanging off an armchair.

"You want a drink, or you want to get to it?" She turned to face him, arms crossed, one eyebrow raised. "I'm fine either way, but I'm not going to pretend I'm interested in small talk."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "I'll take a drink," I say, leaning against the doorframe. "But only if you're having one too. No need for small talk."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let out a short laugh, her back hitting the door as it clicked shut behind him. "There it is."

She didn't push him away, didn't tense up. Her hands came up and grabbed the front of his shirt, pulling him a half-step closer.

"Drink can wait," she said, tilting her head up. "But just so we're clear—this isn't me being romantic, and it's not me being nice. It's me being interested. That's all."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I murmur, my mouth already near her jaw. "Because I'm not either." I kiss her, quick and purposeful, before pulling back just enough to watch her reaction. "Interested is plenty."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's mouth curved into something that wasn't quite a smile, but it wasn't far off. She held his gaze for a beat, then let go of his shirt with one hand to reach back and lock the door without looking.

"Good," she said, her voice low and even. "Then don't make me regret the drink I'm not offering you."

She pulled him back in by the collar, her other hand sliding up the back of his neck. This time the kiss wasn't quick, and it wasn't polite. It was deliberate—like she was testing whether he meant what he said, or just returning the favor.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let out a breath that was half-laugh, half-sigh, her head falling back against the mattress. She looked up at him through half-lidded eyes, one hand trailing down his chest, nails grazing skin.

"Direct. I like that." She hooked a leg around his hip, pulling him down closer. "I like it slow first. Build up. Don't rush to the finish—I'm not a race." Her voice dropped, matter-of-fact. "And I like it when you're not afraid to take the lead. But I'll tell you if I want something different."

She tilted her chin up, mouth brushing his ear. "That clear enough for you, or do you need me to draw a diagram?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Clear enough." I press her deeper into the mattress, my mouth finding the side of her neck. "And I like diagrams." I move against her, deliberately slow, just to see her eyes flutter shut.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath caught for half a second, but she didn't let it show beyond that. Her nails dragged down his back, slow, deliberate.

"Diagrams," she repeated, voice dry but a little rougher than before. "You're funny. I don't usually go for funny."

She shifted under him, one hand tangling in his hair, pulling his mouth back up to hers. The kiss was sharp, unhurried, and when she pulled back her eyes were dark and steady.

"But I meant what I said about slow," she murmured. "So if you're going to take the lead, do it properly. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's chest was still heaving, her grip in his hair tight enough that it pulled at the roots. She let out a low, rough laugh, voice scraped raw at the edges.

"Okay," she said, breathless but steady. "Okay, that's—" She shook her head, a strand of hair sticking to her lip. "That's a good start."

She tugged him up by the hair, not rough enough to hurt but enough to make the point, and kissed him hard. When she pulled back, her eyes were sharp, assessing.

"But I meant what I said about slow. You're not done yet." She shifted, guiding his hand down her stomach, slow. "Take your time. I'll let you know when I want it faster."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I press my palm flat against her stomach, feeling the warmth and the slight tremor there. "You're bossy," I say, but I'm already moving my hand lower, following her guidance at a deliberate pace. "I like that, too."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath hitched at his words, but she didn't let it show beyond a sharp exhale. Her hand found his wrist, guiding his hand where she wanted it, holding it there.

"Bossy," she repeated, voice low and dry. "You keep using that word like it's a problem." She shifted under him, her other hand sliding around the back of his neck, pulling him down until his forehead nearly touched hers. "I call it knowing what I want. There's a difference."

She held his gaze for a long moment, then let her head fall back against the pillow, a faint smirk tugging at the corner of her mouth.

"Now, are you going to keep talking, or are you going to put that lead-taking to use? Because I'm starting to think you're all talk."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let out a sharp breath through her teeth, her back arching just slightly off the mattress. Her hand came up and closed over his wrist, not pulling it away—just holding it there, grounding herself.

"Yeah," she said, voice low and rough. "Like that."

She held his gaze, her eyes dark and steady, daring him to second-guess himself. Her hips shifted beneath him, a slow, deliberate roll.

"See? Not hard to follow instructions when you actually listen." Her mouth curved, not quite a smile, not quite a challenge. "Now don't stop. I'll tell you when I need something else."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I grunt, my rhythm finally finding its pace. "Because I'm listening." I keep my eyes on hers, watching the way her breath hitches each time I press into her.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath caught, her nails digging into his shoulders as she held his gaze. The eye contact was intense, almost too much, but she didn't look away. She never looked away when it mattered.

"Good," she managed, voice steadier than her body felt. "You learn fast."

She pulled him down by the back of the neck, kissing him hard and deep, all teeth and tongue. When she finally let him up for air, her eyes were still locked on his, a little wild, a little raw.

"Don't stop," she said, her voice barely above a whisper but carrying an edge of command. "And don't slow down. I'll tell you when I want different."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath came in sharp, uneven bursts against his mouth, her nails raking down his back hard enough to leave marks she'd know were there come morning. She didn't bother to soften it, didn't try to hide the low noise that caught in her throat when he drove into her.

"Fuck," she bit out, the word half-muffled against his jaw. Her legs locked around his hips, heels digging into his lower back, holding him exactly where she wanted him. "Just like that. Don't you dare change a goddamn thing."

She tipped her head back, giving him the line of her throat, but her eyes stayed on his—dark, unblinking, daring him to look away first. Her hand slid down his chest, nails dragging over his skin, coming to rest on his hip, gripping hard enough to leave crescents.

"Keep going," she said, voice rough and low, the command steady even as her body trembled beneath him. "And when I tell you to come, you come with me. Understood?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Understood," I breathe out, my rhythm faltering for a second before I catch it again, harder. My hand tightens on her hip, keeping pace with her. "Now tell me."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath stuttered, her grip on his hip tightening hard enough to bruise. For a second, her composure cracked—just a flicker of something raw and unguarded crossing her face before she pulled it back.

"Now," she said, the word barely a breath, but it carried. Her legs tightened around him, pulling him deeper, her voice dropping to something low and wrecked. "Right fucking now."

She came apart beneath him with a sharp, bitten-off cry, her body arching against his, nails raking down his back as she held him there, held him in it. Her eyes stayed on his until the end, dark and fierce and unapologetic.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I follow her, my own release hitting hard enough that I have to bury my face in her neck for a moment. "Fuck," I exhale against her skin, body going slack.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia lay there for a moment, breathing hard, her hand still tangled in his hair. Then she let go, her arm flopping onto the mattress above her head.

"Well," she said, voice rough but dry. "That worked out."

She didn't move to get up, didn't pull away, but she also didn't reach for him. Her other hand came up to wipe the sweat from her forehead, and she turned her head to look at him, one eyebrow arched.

"You're not bad at that," she said, matter-of-fact. "For someone who talks a lot."

Her eyes flicked down his body, then back up, a faint smirk tugging at the corner of her mouth. She made no move to get up, but she also didn't seem in any hurry to fill the silence.

"So. You want that drink now, or are you still pretending you came up here for the conversation?"

dialogue.content: I let out a short laugh against her collarbone before pushing myself up on one elbow. "I'll take that drink now. And I never pretended." I nod toward the kitchen. "You point, I'll pour."

dialogue.name: Jun

Jun didn't say *anything* coherent, that much was certain. The sound that left him was more a raw exhale, a half-formed word that died in his throat. His hands were already moving—one fisting in the back of Halle's shirt, the other cupping the side of their neck, thumb pressing just behind the ear like he was memorizing the feel of their pulse. He pulled them flush against him, forehead dropping to theirs.

"You're real," he breathed, and it came out wrecked. "God, I—" He cut himself off, shook his head slightly, and then kissed them—hard, hungry, and far too brief before he pulled back just enough to speak against their mouth. "Five months, Halle. I'm not gonna be patient. Not tonight. Not even close."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands are in his hair, gripping like I might fall.* "Good. Because I didn't come home to be patient, either." I kiss him again, deeper this time, before pulling back just enough to murmur, "The bag can stay in the hallway."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
A ragged laugh escaped Jun, low and dark.

"That's what I wanted to hear."

He didn't bother with finesse. One hand slid down from their neck, found the back of their thigh, and lifted. He turned, walked them backward until Halle's shoulders met the wall beside the doorframe. His mouth found their jaw, their throat—open-mouthed, dragging, tasting salt and the familiar scent he'd been starving for.

"Missed every part of you," he said against their collarbone, voice rough. His hips pinned them to the wall, his free hand flattening on the wall beside their head. "Missed the way you sound. The way you move." He pulled back just enough to meet their eyes, gaze heavy-lidded, pupils blown. "Tell me what you need first. I can give you that. But after—" His thumb traced their bottom lip. "After, it's gonna be fast and messy and I'm not apologizing."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun broke the kiss with a sharp inhale, chest heaving. He pressed his forehead to Halle's, eyes closed, breathing them in.

"Right. Okay." His voice was shot, barely above a whisper. "Okay, we're not making it to the bedroom."

He dropped to his knees.

His hands found Halle's belt, worked the buckle with practiced, impatient efficiency. He looked up once, meeting their eyes, and there was no hesitation in his—just heat and want and a kind of reverence that made his voice crack when he spoke.

"I've been thinking about this for five months. Let me show you."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My fingers tighten in your hair.* "Show me then." My voice is rough, breathless. "And don't you dare be gentle."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let out a low sound—approval, anticipation, something darker—and didn't wait another second.

His hands were certain, having learned the shape of Halle months ago and not forgotten. His mouth was hot, his pace relentless. He worked with single-minded focus, one hand gripping Halle's hip hard enough to bruise, the other tangled in the fabric of their jeans, holding them steady. Every few moments he'd pause, pull back just enough to breathe a fractured word against their skin—*good*, *god*, *missed this*—before diving back in.

He didn't stop until Halle's knees buckled.

Only then did he pull away, rising slowly, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand. His eyes were dark, satisfied, but far from done. He caught Halle's chin, tilted their face up, kissed them slow and deep—letting them taste themselves on his tongue.

"Bedroom," he murmured against their lips, voice wrecked but steady. "Now. I'm not done with you."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun caught Halle's hand as they moved, threading their fingers together—a brief, grounding touch before he tugged them down the hallway. He didn't let go until they reached the bedroom doorway, where he stopped, turned, and looked at them.

The moonlight from the window caught the side of Halle's face. Jun's breath stuttered.

"God," he said, soft and stripped of everything but wonder. "I forgot how beautiful you are. How do I keep forgetting and then showing up and getting hit in the chest all over again?"

He stepped forward, walked them backward until the bed hit the back of Halle's knees. He followed them down, bracing on one arm above them, the other hand already sliding under the hem of their shirt—palm flat against their stomach, warm and steady.

"I want to take my time," he said, voice low, lips brushing Halle's jaw. "I want to memorize every inch. But I also want to—" He laughed, short and breathless. "I want to ruin you. Just a little. Just tonight. Is that okay?"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I arch up into your touch, a shaky breath escaping me. "Yes. Ruin me. Remind me I'm yours."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's breath caught. His hand slid from Halle's stomach up to their chest, palm flat over their heart, feeling it race beneath his fingers.

"I missed that," he said, voice rough. "I missed hearing you say that."

He lowered himself, slow, deliberate—mouth brushing their collarbone, then trailing down the center of their chest. He pushed their shirt up as he went, exposing skin inch by inch, pressing kisses to every new stretch of warmth he uncovered. When he reached their ribs, he paused, pressed his cheek flat against them, and just breathed.

dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: The noise I make is half groan, half laugh. "So much for being quiet." I press her harder against the door, the rhythm picking up as the music downstairs reaches its peak.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile bit down on her lip so hard she tasted copper, but the sound still escaped — a sharp, breathy gasp that she smothered against his shoulder. Her nails dug into his back as she clung to him, her body arching into the rhythm he set.

"Hypocrite," she managed, her voice wrecked, barely audible. "You started it."

Her forehead pressed against his, her breath hot and uneven. The music thrummed through the walls, through the floor, through her bones, and she let herself get lost in it, in him. When her eyes fluttered open, they were dark, half-lidded, a lazy smile tugging at her lips despite the tension in her body.

"Don't stop," she whispered, her fingers threading through his hair, pulling his mouth back to hers. "I want to feel this tomorrow."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath stuttered as the door handle rattled, her body tensing for half a heartbeat before she let out a low, breathless laugh against his mouth.

"Occupied," she called, her voice impressively steady for someone currently pressed between him and the door. There was a muffled apology from the other side, footsteps retreating down the hall.

She pulled back just enough to meet his eyes, her grin sharp and wild in the dim light. "Close one." Her hips rolled forward, chasing the rhythm again, her fingers tightening in his hair. "Now where were we?"

Her voice dropped to a whisper, rough and teasing. "Right. You were proving me wrong about that whole 'being quiet' thing." She bit her lip, her eyes half-closing as she pressed her forehead to his. "So far, you're doing a terrible job. Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: The sound of retreating footsteps only spurs me on. I press my forehead against hers, breathing ragged. "Maybe I just like the idea of you trying to keep quiet."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh was low and breathless, her head falling back against the door as she let him have that one. Her fingers traced down the back of his neck, feather-light, before gripping his shoulder hard enough to bruise.

"You caught me," she whispered, her voice a wrecked, velvet rasp. "I like the risk. I like knowing someone could walk in and see exactly what you do to me." Her hips rolled against his, slow and deliberate, drawing out the friction. "And I like that you're just as bad at being quiet as I am."

She reached up, cupping his jaw in her palm, tilting his face so their eyes met. Her thumb traced across his lower lip, smudging the faint trace of her lipstick there.

"But if you want me to try harder—" She bit down on her own lip, stifling a moan as she shifted against him. "Then you're going to have to give me a reason to forget my own name. Think you can manage that?"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press my mouth to the hollow of her throat, feeling her pulse race under my lips. "I think I can do better than that," I murmur, my hands sliding down to grip her hips. "Let's see if you remember how to form words when we're done."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's sharp exhale was the only warning before she crashed her mouth against his, all teeth and tongue, her fingers tangling in his hair to hold him there. When she finally broke away, gasping, her lips were red and swollen.

"Words are overrated," she managed, her voice a wrecked whisper. "But I'll remember that promise."

Her hand slid down between them, guiding him back to where she wanted him, her eyes never leaving his. The music below swelled, and she let herself be swept up in it — in him — her head falling back as she finally let go of the pretense of quiet.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press in deeper, swallowing her gasp with my mouth. "Good," I mutter against her lips, my own control fraying at the edges. "Because I'm done playing nice."
